case_title: M. Nageswara Reddy v. The State of Andhra Pradesh and Others
accused_victim_relationship: Political rivals/prior enmity: the High Court described the accused as members of a rival faction; the accused's defence was political rivalry and past enmity
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW1, PW3, PW5); injured eyewitness testimony (PW6, PW7); medical and documentary evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Per prosecution case: multiple assailants armed with hunting sickles, indiscriminate hacking of the victim, and injuries to the driver and another occupant
trial_court_outcome: Accused 1-3 convicted under ss.148 and 302 IPC; life imprisonment (s.302) and one year RI (s.148). Accused 4-11 acquitted of all charges
high_court_outcome: Appeal of accused 1-3 allowed; their conviction reversed and they were acquitted. Complainant's appeal against acquittal of accused 4-11 dismissed
offence_finally_established: Accused 1-3: IPC s.302 (murder) and s.148 (rioting with deadly weapon)
neutral_facts: On an evening in January 2007, at about 8:30 p.m., a group of eleven accused persons, armed with hunting sickles, allegedly emerged from behind a sumo vehicle and surrounded it near a clinic in Kurnool. The vehicle was carrying the victim, the victim's brother, other occupants and a driver. Three of the accused allegedly forcibly opened the front left door, dragged the victim out, and hacked him repeatedly with hunting sickles, causing his death on the spot. Other accused allegedly struck the vehicle's glass windows with sickles and broke them. Two accused allegedly hacked the driver, causing bleeding injuries to his shoulder, hand and ribs. Further accused allegedly chased the fleeing occupants, and one occupant was injured. The injured driver and another injured occupant were taken to hospital. A first information report was lodged on the statement of the victim's brother, and the investigating officer recorded witness statements, collected medical and documentary evidence, and arrested the accused. The prosecution relied on the testimony of three eyewitnesses, two injured eyewitnesses and the medical evidence. The accused denied the charges.
physical_harm: Victim killed by hacking with hunting sickles; driver (PW6) suffered bleeding injuries to right shoulder, hand and side ribs; PW7 injured while fleeing
number_of_offences: 7 charged; 2 finally upheld (ss.148 and 302 IPC, accused 1-3)
financial_property_loss: Damage to vehicle windows (charged under s.427 IPC); no monetary value stated
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness identification of accused 1-3 by PW1, PW3 and PW6; testimony of injured eyewitnesses PW6 and PW7; the incident as proved by PW7's deposition; FIR lodged within seven hours and sent to Magistrate within 24 hours
witness_credibility: Court found no material contradictions among eyewitnesses and injured eyewitnesses regarding accused 1-3. Relationship to the deceased did not by itself discredit PW1, PW3, PW5. PW6, as injured eyewitness, had greater reliability. High Court's reasons (minor contradictions, planted witnesses) were held unwarranted. PW7 could not identify assailants but the incident was proved through his evidence
trial_duration: offence: 18.01.2007; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 21.02.2018; Supreme Court: 07.03.2022
legal_representation: For appellants (original complainant and State): A. Sirajudeen, Sr. Adv., with others. For respondents (original accused): Guntur Prabhakar, D. Ramakrishna Reddy and others
investigation_status: FIR registered as Crime No. 7 of 2007; investigation completed; chargesheet filed against all eleven accused; case committed to Sessions Court
procedural_irregularity: Alleged interpolation of time in FIR and seven-hour delay in lodging FIR. Court held not fatal: point not raised at trial, not put to investigating officers, and FIR sent to Magistrate within 24 hours
appeal_history: Trial court: accused 1-3 convicted under ss.148 and 302 IPC (life imprisonment); accused 4-11 acquitted. High Court: accused 1-3 acquitted; complainant's appeal against accused 4-11 dismissed. Supreme Court: appeals 72/2022 and 74/2022 allowed, trial court conviction of accused 1-3 restored; appeal 73/2022 dismissed
prosecution_argument: High Court wrongly gave weight to alleged FIR time interpolation, which was not raised at trial or put to investigating officers; FIR sent to Magistrate within 24 hours as required; eyewitness and injured eyewitness testimony consistent; minor contradictions not material; relatives not interested witnesses merely by relationship; High Court failed to reappreciate PW5's evidence; injuries supported by medical evidence
defence_argument: FIR time altered from 0.30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.; seven-hour delay and FIR reaching Magistrate at 4:30 a.m. despite short distance; so FIR and testimony of PW1, PW3, PW6 and PW7 were properly disbelieved and accused falsely implicated
legal_principle_applied: Relatives' evidence not discarded merely because they are relatives; injured eyewitness testimony has greater reliability; delay in lodging FIR not fatal absent material prejudice; first appellate court must reappreciate all evidence; concurrent acquittals not interfered with where plausible; roles of accused compared individually
precedent_relied_upon: Not stated (court refers generally to a line of decisions on injured eyewitnesses without naming any case)
other_sentence_order: Accused 1-3 directed to surrender within four weeks to undergo the remaining sentence
